one_line: Privacy-preserving browser workout coach that exposes live pose-derived metrics to an AI agent.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent structured live metrics and phase-scoped workout controls without exposing camera frames, enabling reliable coaching against shared page state.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies seven imperative tools plus one declarative form on document.modelContext.
Read tools expose live metrics and set history; writes are gesture-gated and registrations change by workout phase.
Frame sheets show agent plan creation, set start, countdown, live rep counting, and a proposed adjustment.
Devpost screenshot shows an agent log alongside pushup metrics and form flags.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent plan-to-set-to-metrics-to-adjustment flow with substantial visual coverage, though no continuous video was submitted and some later claims rely on packaging.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show generated plan, countdown, rep counts, live pose tracking, history, and approval modal.
Screenshot visibly shows Pushup session controls, rep count, hip sag/elbow flare flags, and agent activity.
Demo link is reported alive and seven gallery images exist.
impact_rationale: Home exercisers have a concrete safety and coaching need; on-device numeric coaching credibly addresses privacy concerns while providing form feedback.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies home-workout injury risk and the privacy problem of sending video to AI services.
Visible workflow demonstrates rep counting and form flags rather than only describing them.

usability_note: The demonstrated controls and metrics are legible and appropriate for exercising, though camera setup and gesture recognition are not independently observed.
red_flags: No submitted video; visual evidence is frame-sheet/gallery based.
Some claims about privacy and gesture reliability are not independently verifiable from screenshots.
standouts: Agent and human share workout state with consequential writes gated.
advance_reason: High-leverage, well-evidenced health workflow with a distinctive privacy and human-control design.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central: narrow page tools operate on the same live versioned state, enforce authority boundaries, reject stale writes atomically, and expose auditable simulation receipts.

Frame sheets show six discovered tools for snapshot, scenario creation, changes, simulation, and comparison.
Transcript documents STALE_FACTORY rejection after a human lock and fresh replanning.
Capability map visibly separates AVAILABLE, HUMAN_LOCKED, and PHASE_CLOSED controls.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a deeply coherent end-to-end factory workflow with explicit constraints, scenario comparison, stale-state handling, and an infeasibility proof.
execution_evidence: Transcript reports two simulated scenarios, constraint outcomes, and immutable receipts.
Transcript shows atomic stale-write rejection with no state mutation, then fresh post-lock planning.
Frame sheets show factory workspace, tool registry, capability map, and completed replay.
Demo is reported alive with a 177-second video.
impact_rationale: Factory planners and operations teams have a real coordination and decision-audit problem; the system credibly improves safe replanning, although the demo uses fictional data.
impact_evidence: Mission has concrete output, cost, machine, and defect constraints.
Transcript emphasizes fragmented factory planning and authority loss across handoffs.
Receipt-backed comparison and proven infeasibility directly support operational decisions.
creativity_rationale: Versioned shared state, authority-aware capabilities, atomic stale-write rejection, and deterministic proof of infeasibility form a notably original agent interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Human lock changes the capability map and invalidates old writes.

standouts: Atomic stale-write handling plus receipt-backed infeasibility proof.

Frame sheets show all major lifecycle states and provider exclusion reasoning.
Devpost screenshot shows natural-language request with no tool names and approval constraint.
About text reports reset verification and exact five-tool baseline.
impact_rationale: Service coordinators face fragmented records and consequential dispatch authority; the workflow credibly reduces dropped constraints while preserving human control.
impact_evidence: Request combines qualification, history, budget, deadline, and no-submit condition.
Provider comparison visibly explains exclusion of cheaper/unqualified or late candidates.
Description grounds the pattern in firsthand service operations, while not claiming adoption.

usability_note: The staged lifecycle is clear and operationally appropriate, though the dense evidence/dashboard presentation may be more technical than end users need.
